info.title: PowerApps Advisor API (Solution Checker)
info.description:
Unofficial. The PowerApps Advisor API (api.advisor.powerapps.com) is the service behind Power Platform solution checker: it publishes the rule catalogue and runs static analysis over uploaded solution files. Every environment advertises its own regional advisor endpoint in its runtime endpoints (PowerAppsAdvisor), so the host is per-geography, not global.

Two sources fed this spec. The rule and ruleset reads were reverse-engineered from live traffic against a real tenant across all 17 public-cloud geographies and are marked x-probe-verified: true; their schemas, enums, optionality and error bodies are what the service actually returned. The analysis job flow (upload, analyze, status) is transcribed from Microsoft's public documentation and is marked x-probe-verified: false, because verifying it end to end would mean submitting real analysis jobs against a production tenant. The existence, HTTP method and api-version of those three routes were confirmed non-destructively; their request and response bodies were not.

The Terraform provider microsoft/terraform-provider-power-platform (internal/clients/advisor) consumes exactly one of these operations, GET /api/rule for the solution checker ruleset, and models nine of the fields it returns.

Two api-versions coexist: 2.0 for the catalogue reads, 1.0 for the analysis job flow. Sending the wrong one is rejected as an unsupported version rather than treated as a missing route, which is how the unprobed routes were confirmed to exist.

servers.description: Per-geography host. Take it from the environment's PowerAppsAdvisor runtime endpoint rather than composing it: the mapping from an environment's location to its advisor region is not a string transform. All 17 listed regions were reached live with the same token.

region.description: Public-cloud geographies confirmed to serve this API. Sovereign clouds (US Government, China, DoD) use different hostnames and were not probed.

tags.name: Rules
tags.description: The checker rule catalogue. A rule is one static-analysis check over a solution component - a plug-in registration, a canvas app formula, a JavaScript web resource, a desktop flow - carrying a severity, a category and a link to published guidance. The catalogue is read-only and published per geography; it is what the report's issue titles, severities and guidance links are resolved from.

tags.name: Rulesets
tags.description: Named groupings of rules. A rule may belong to no ruleset, one, or several, and a ruleset id is what an analysis run is configured with - it is the unit of 'which standard am I being checked against'. The public cloud publishes two: Solution Checker, the everyday set used by the maker portal and by Managed Environments enforcement, and AppSource Certification, the stricter set a solution must pass to be listed on AppSource.

tags.name: Analysis
tags.description: The asynchronous static-analysis job. A run uploads solution files to blob storage, submits a job naming those files and a ruleset, polls for completion, and downloads a SARIF v2 report per file. Documented by Microsoft; not probed here, because exercising it means submitting real jobs against a real tenant.

get.description:
Reads the rule catalogue from one environment's advisor endpoint, optionally narrowed to one or more rulesets. Resolve the host from the environment's PowerAppsAdvisor runtime endpoint; the catalogue is not tenant- or environment-specific beyond that, so any environment in a geography answers identically.

The response is a flat JSON array with no envelope, pagination or total count - the whole catalogue arrives in one body, around 100 rules and 40 KB, four times that with message formats.

Two behaviours matter before relying on this endpoint. First, the ruleset parameter fails open: an unrecognised id or name is not rejected, it yields the single rule that belongs to no ruleset (web-unsupported-syntax), so a typo silently produces a near-empty catalogue rather than an error. An empty, whitespace or bare-comma value behaves like omitting the parameter entirely and returns every rule.

Second, the catalogue is not identical across geographies, despite the Terraform provider client's comment that it is. At time of probing the Solution Checker ruleset returned 98 rules in unitedstates and australia and 89 in the other 15 public geographies - the nine web-sdl-* security rules had reached only two deployment rings. Anything that diffs, caches or pins this catalogue must key by region.

Rule text is localised by Accept-Language; code, guidanceUrl, severity and primaryCategory are invariant across languages.

parameters.name: api-version
parameters.description: Optional in practice - omitting it serves the same payload as 2.0. The Terraform provider always sends 2.0.

parameters.name: ruleset
parameters.description: Ruleset id or display name, matched case-insensitively, or several separated by comma or semicolon - in which case the response is their union, not their concatenation (103 rules for both public rulesets, which overlap heavily, not 98 + 64). Omit to get every rule the geography publishes. Unrecognised values fail open rather than erroring; see the operation description. There is no service-side default: omitted means every rule, not Solution Checker.

solutionCheckerById.summary: Solution Checker by id (what the Terraform provider sends)

parameters.name: includeMessageFormats
parameters.description: Adds messageTemplates to every rule, which roughly quadruples the response size and its processing time - ask for it only when pre-translating report output. Parsed strictly as a boolean, unlike ruleset, so a junk value is rejected.

200.description: The matching rules, as a top-level array. Also the response to an unrecognised ruleset value, with one element. Microsoft documents a 204 for 'no results were found'; no input produced one.

400.description: Either an api-version other than 1.0 or 2.0, which returns ErrorResponse with code UnsupportedApiVersion, or a query parameter value that fails model binding - a non-boolean includeMessageFormats - which returns ValidationProblemDetails naming the offending parameter. The two bodies are structurally unrelated, so a client that parses errors must handle both.

401.description: No or invalid bearer token. Microsoft's documentation states the rule and ruleset reads need no OAuth token; live they do. The WWW-Authenticate challenge names the resource to request a token for, so an unauthenticated call is a legitimate way to discover the audience.

405.description: Any method other than GET. The Allow header names GET and the body is an ErrorResponse, confusingly also coded UnsupportedApiVersion.

get.description:
Reads every ruleset the geography publishes, as a flat array of id and name with no envelope or pagination. Resolve the host from the environment's PowerAppsAdvisor runtime endpoint. Call this to discover the ruleset id to pass to a rule listing or an analysis run, though in practice the two public ids are stable enough to hard-code, which is what the Terraform provider does.

The same two rulesets were returned by all 17 public geographies at time of probing. They overlap rather than nest: AppSource Certification has five rules Solution Checker does not, and Solution Checker has 39 that AppSource Certification does not.

Names are not localised - an Accept-Language of fr still returns English names, unlike rule text. Note also that Microsoft's own rule documentation labels 083a2ef5-7e0e-4754-9d88-9455142dc08b 'Solution Checker' in its examples; the service says that id is AppSource Certification. Trust the service.

parameters.name: api-version
parameters.description: Optional. 1.0 and 2.0 both serve the same payload.

200.description: The rulesets, as a top-level array.

400.description: An api-version other than 1.0 or 2.0, as ErrorResponse with code UnsupportedApiVersion.

401.description: No or invalid bearer token, with the same WWW-Authenticate challenge the rule listing returns.

405.description: Any method other than GET; the Allow header names GET.

post.description:
Uploads one solution zip to service-managed blob storage in the geography, so that the analysis job that follows has a URI it can read the solution from. This step is optional: any Azure blob SAS URI the service can reach works just as well, and must be used for files above the 30 MB limit. Upload files in parallel, one call each, all under the same x-ms-correlation-id as the analyze call that will name them.

Not probed - uploading writes to the service. What was verified non-destructively is that the route exists, is served at api-version 1.0 only, and accepts POST alone. The request and responses below are transcribed from Microsoft's documentation.

requestBody.description: multipart/form-data. Content-Disposition must carry both name and filename, e.g. form-data; name="solution.zip"; filename="solution.zip" - the filename is what identifies the file in the report.

schema.description: The solution zip, as a single form part.

file.description: The solution zip, at most 30 MB.

400.description: The content was not a zip, the parameters were wrong, or the file failed the service's virus scan. No response body distinguishes the three.

413.description: Larger than 30 MB. Upload to your own storage and pass a SAS URI to the analysis run instead.

post.description:
Submits a static-analysis job over one or more uploaded solution files and returns immediately with a status URL in the Location header; the work itself typically takes one to five minutes. Poll that URL at 15 to 60 second intervals rather than tightly.

x-ms-correlation-id is the job's identity, not merely a trace header: the same value ties the uploads, this submission and the status polls of one run together, and resubmitting with a value already used is refused. Configure the run with either ruleSets or ruleCodes, not both.

Not probed - submitting a job is a real write against a real tenant. Verified non-destructively: the route exists, is served at api-version 1.0 only, and accepts POST alone. The body and responses below are transcribed from Microsoft's documentation.

202.description: The job was accepted and is running. No response body; the Location header is the only thing that matters.

Location.description: Status URL for this job, of the form https://{region}.api.advisor.powerapps.com/api/status/{analysisId}?api-version=1.0.

400.description: Non-zip content behind one of the SAS URIs, bad parameters, or a file that failed virus scanning. No response body.

409.description: The x-ms-correlation-id has already been used for a job. Generate a fresh GUID per run rather than retrying with the same one.

get.description:
Polls a submitted job, following the URL the submission put in its Location header. While the job runs the response reports progress; once it finishes the same shape gains resultFileUris - one short-lived SAS download URI per submitted file, each a zip containing a SARIF v2 report - and issueSummary, the per-severity finding counts. Poll at 15 to 60 second intervals, carrying the run's x-ms-correlation-id, and use a token for the same client application that submitted the job.

Partially probed. Live-confirmed: the route exists and is served at api-version 1.0 only; an unauthenticated call is refused with the same challenge as the catalogue reads; an unknown job id is reported as problem+json, a different error shape from the rest of this API. One quirk worth guarding against: the all-zeros GUID is not handled as an id at all and faults the service rather than returning not-found, so never use it as a placeholder here. The success bodies below are transcribed from Microsoft's documentation - reaching them requires a real job.

parameters.name: analysisId
parameters.description: The job id, taken from the Location header of the submission rather than constructed. In practice the same GUID as the run's x-ms-correlation-id.

200.description: The job has finished - successfully or not, so read status rather than assuming success - and resultFileUris and issueSummary are populated. Stop polling.

202.description: Still running. Same body shape without the result fields; wait and poll the same URL again.

400.description: An api-version other than 1.0 - this route is not served at 2.0 - as ErrorResponse with code UnsupportedApiVersion.

403.description: The token belongs to a different client application than the one that submitted the job. Results are readable only by the submitter.

404.description: No such analysis job - unknown id, or one that has aged out. Served as application/problem+json, not the ErrorResponse envelope the api-version errors use. An analysisId that is not a GUID at all gets a bare 404 with no body instead, from routing rather than from the operation.

500.description: Observed only for the all-zeros GUID, which the service appears to treat as an unset value rather than an unknown id. Empty body, and unaffected by the request headers. Any other GUID returns a clean not-found, so do not use the zero GUID as a probe or placeholder.

azure_auth.description: Microsoft Entra ID OAuth2. The audience is the advisor service itself, not the PowerApps service - the challenge on an unauthenticated call names resource_id https://api.advisor.powerapps.com/.

AcceptLanguage.name: Accept-Language
AcceptLanguage.description: Language for the human-readable rule text, defaulting to en-US. Verified live: fr localises summary, description and howToFix while code, guidanceUrl, severity and primaryCategory stay invariant. Ruleset names are not localised at all. Multiple languages may be listed, the first being primary.

ApiVersion10.name: api-version
ApiVersion10.description: The analysis job routes are served at 1.0 only, unlike the catalogue reads which are 2.0. Sending 2.0 here is rejected as an unsupported version, which is how these routes were confirmed to exist without invoking them.

TenantIdHeader.name: x-ms-tenant-id
TenantIdHeader.description: Tenant the analysed solution belongs to.

CorrelationIdHeader.name: x-ms-correlation-id
CorrelationIdHeader.description: The identity of one analysis run: send the same freshly generated GUID on every upload, the submission and every status poll of that run. Reusing one on a later submission is refused as a duplicate.

Rule.description: One checker rule: what it looks for, how bad a violation is, and where the guidance for fixing it lives. Live responses carry exactly these nine fields - no envelope, no @odata metadata, no pagination. Only code, guidanceUrl, include, componentType, primaryCategory and severity are present on every rule: description, summary and howToFix are absent entirely on rules with no authored text (observed on web-unsupported-syntax), and howToFix is an empty string on roughly half the rest. Microsoft's documentation shows howToFix as an object with a summary property; at api-version 2.0 the service returns a plain string. No property was ever observed explicitly null across 1531 rule objects (both rulesets, all 17 geographies) - absent means absent.

code.description: Stable rule identifier, and the rule id findings are reported under in the SARIF report. Prefixed by the component family it analyses: app- (canvas apps), connector- (custom connectors), desktopflow- (Power Automate desktop flows), flow- (cloud flows), meta- (plug-ins, workflow activities and solution metadata), web- (JavaScript web resources).

summary.description: One-line title of the rule, as shown in the solution checker report's Issue column. Localised by Accept-Language.

description.description: Longer statement of what the rule checks for. Localised by Accept-Language. Note this describes the check, not a particular finding - per-finding text comes from messageTemplates.

guidanceUrl.description: Published guidance explaining the issue and the recommended fix - the report's Guidance link. Either a learn.microsoft.com article or a go.microsoft.com fwlink redirect carrying the rule code in its error query parameter. Never empty in any observed response, though a link may resolve to a general best-practices page rather than a dedicated article.

howToFix.description: Short remediation instruction shown alongside a finding. Authored for only about half the rules; an empty string where there is none.

include.description: Whether the rule participates in an analysis run. True on every rule this endpoint returns - the catalogue only lists included rules - so it is not usable as a filter. It carries meaning in a SARIF report, where an excluded rule can appear as false.

componentType.description: Undocumented, and 0 on every one of the 1531 rule objects probed, so no mapping to solution component types can be established from live data - the enum below records what the service returns, not the full domain. The component family a rule targets is instead readable from its code prefix.

primaryCategory.description: What kind of problem the rule looks for: 1 Performance, 2 Upgrade Readiness (patterns that risk breaking on a platform version upgrade), 3 Usage (misuse of an API, pattern or configuration), 4 Security, 5 Design, 7 Maintainability, 8 Supportability (use of removed, unpublished or otherwise unsupported APIs), 9 Accessibility, 10 licensing entitlement (the meta-license-* rules; this category has no published name). The numbering is not the order of the category list published under model-driven app best practices - it was derived by cross-referencing 38 rule codes against their documented category names, with no collisions. 6 was never returned by any geography and is presumed to be Online Migration, the one documented category with no live rule.

severity.description: Impact ranking, ascending: 1 Informational, 2 Low, 3 Medium, 4 High, 5 Critical. Names are confirmed by cross-referencing 38 rule codes against their documented severities on Microsoft Learn; 2-5 were observed live, 1 was not. Critical is the level solution checker enforcement blocks a solution import on in Managed Environments, so it is the one with governance consequences rather than only advisory weight. The same five levels are the buckets in IssueSummary.

messageTemplates.description: The message variations this rule can emit, intended for pre-translating report output. Present and non-empty on every rule when the request asks for message formats, and absent entirely otherwise - so unlike howToFix, there is no rule without message text.

MessageTemplate.description: One message variation a rule can emit - the per-finding wording that appears in a SARIF report, as opposed to the rule's own fixed summary. Returned only when the request asks for message formats.

ruleId.description: The owning rule's code, repeated on every template.

messageTemplateId.description: Identifier a SARIF finding references to select this variation. Usually message1, message2 and so on, numbered per rule, but not guaranteed to follow that form - descriptive ids such as connectiontoconnectionreferencemode also occur.

messageTemplate.description: Format string whose positional {0}, {1}, ... placeholders are filled from the arguments the SARIF finding carries. Translate the template, not the assembled message.

Ruleset.description: A named grouping of rules - the standard a solution is checked against. Both fields are present on every observed response.

id.description: Returned lowercase, and accepted case-insensitively wherever a ruleset is named. Stable across geographies: 0ad12346-e108-40b8-a956-9a8f95ea18c9 is Solution Checker and 083a2ef5-7e0e-4754-9d88-9455142dc08b is AppSource Certification.

name.description: Display name, also accepted in place of the id when naming a ruleset. Not localised.

AnalysisRequest.description: Configuration for one analysis run: what to analyse, against which rules, and what to skip. Supply exactly one of ruleSets or ruleCodes. Documented shape; not probed.

sasUriList.description: Blob URIs the service can download without further credentials - either those produced by the upload step or your own SAS URIs. Each may be a single solution, a zip of several, or a package, and each produces one entry in resultFileUris.

ruleSets.description: Rulesets to check against, normally exactly one. The usual choice over naming individual rules.

ruleCodes.description: Individual rules to check, as an alternative to whole rulesets when you want a narrower run.

fileExclusions.description: File names or patterns to skip, typically third-party libraries you did not write and cannot fix. A * wildcard is supported at either end, e.g. *jquery* or *jquery.dll.

RulesetReference.description: Names one ruleset for an analysis run to check against.

id.description: A ruleset id from the ruleset listing.

RuleReference.description: Names one individual rule for an analysis run to check.

code.description: A rule code from the rule catalogue.

AnalysisStatus.description: The state of one analysis job, and once it has completed, where to fetch its report and how many findings it produced. Documented shape; not probed.

status.description: InProgress while the job runs. Finished on clean completion. FinishedWithErrors means a report exists but one or more rules failed to run, so it may be incomplete - a service-side fault rather than a finding about the solution, and a reason not to gate a release on the counts. Failed means the job itself broke and there is no report.

runCorrelationId.description: Echo of the run's x-ms-correlation-id, for matching a response to a run when several are in flight.

resultFileUris.description: Time-limited SAS download URIs, one per file submitted, present only once processing has completed. Each is a zip containing a SARIF v2 JSON report. Download promptly - the SAS expires.

privacyPolicy.description: Link to the privacy policy covering the analysed content.

IssueSummary.description: Finding counts bucketed by severity, present only once processing has completed. The five buckets are the names behind Rule.severity's numeric values, so criticalIssueCount counts findings from rules with severity 5. Critical is the bucket Managed Environments solution checker enforcement blocks on.

ErrorResponse.description: The envelope used for api-version and HTTP-method negotiation failures - the outermost routing layer, before any operation runs. Distinct from the problem-details shapes the operations themselves return.

ErrorDetail.description: The code and message pair inside an ErrorResponse.

code.description: UnsupportedApiVersion is the only value observed, and it covers both an unsupported api-version and an unsupported method on a supported one - so the code alone does not tell you which.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. It embeds the internal service-fabric node address and partition path of the instance that handled the request, so log it but do not surface it to end users.

ProblemDetails.description: RFC 9110 problem details, served as application/problem+json. Used by the analysis status route; the catalogue reads use ErrorResponse instead.

type.description: Link to the RFC section for the status code, not a service-specific error taxonomy - it carries no diagnostic information.

traceId.description: Kestrel connection and request id, of the form {connectionId}:{requestNumber}. The value to quote when asking support to look up a request.

ValidationProblemDetails.description: Model-binding failure on a query parameter - a value the service could not parse into the expected type. Returned as application/json despite being a problem-details document, unlike ProblemDetails.

errors.description: Parameter name to the list of messages about it, so the caller can point at the offending input.

title.example: One or more validation errors occurred.

traceId.description: Kestrel connection and request id, as in ProblemDetails.
